steady.basis: per active MW (= critical IT MW): $14m revenue (between the 2028 and 2029 vintages; the 2030 fleet average is $13.3m), 60% EBITDA after rent and power (reported 57-59%; mature contracts ~70%), GPUs + ancillaries $33m, no shell (leased), tray-swap refresh 55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr spares, 21% tax, 10.5% WACC; market $/MW +6%/yr for five years then flat; contracted MW reprice at 5-yr renewals, spot at 13%; 95/5 blend

prepay.basis: weighted-average prepayment 15-25% of TCV at signing (424B4/10-K), credited against billings in the final months of the contract; at the 20% midpoint on a 5-yr contract at $14m per MW-yr that is $14m per MW, ~42% of the $33m GPU cost; deferred revenue $9.7bn at 30-Jun-26 (10-Q) is the opening balance, credited half in-window (2028-30) and half after 2030 (OpenAI to May-31, Meta to Dec-32)

finance.wfMarginBasis: the quarterly waterfall runs at the printed 57% adjusted EBITDA margin (Q4-25 to Q2-26: 57/56/59%); the per-MW multiple uses 60%, a mature-MW margin between the print and management’s ~70% contract-level zone
finance.basis: debt 8% (senior notes 9.0-9.75%, DDTL 4.0 SOFR+225/5.9% fixed, DDTL 5.0/5.5 SOFR+450/550, OEM financing; converts 1.75%), 16%/yr pool amortisation (DDTLs amortise over 5 yrs, notes bullet), $3bn cash floor; lenders advance 90% of GPU cost on contracted capacity (DDTL 4.0 90% LTC), 50% on spot; the shell is leased (rent inside EBITDA, no shell capex, lease liabilities not double-counted as debt); 10% of capex from 2027 as policy equity at $90 plus the residual; converts (2031 $2.59bn at $107.80 cap $215.60; 2032 $4.0bn at $119.60 cap $230) convert at the model 2030 price; restricted cash $1.4bn counted; fully diluted count before converts 608.5m = 551.5m basic (31 Jul 26) + 24m options at $1.84 + 4m warrants at $1.55 + 29m RSUs

power: MW active at 30 June · 4.2 GW contracted

notes: 4.2 GW contracted, 1.5 GW active. Fifty-one leased data centres; no single provider delivers more than 17% of active power. Every site is rented — Core Scientific (590 MW), Applied Digital (400 MW), Galaxy Helios (525 MW), Chirisa, TierPoint, Flexential.Q2-26 10-Q · 11 Aug call

The bottleneck is powered shell, not GPUs or grid. One lessor running late cost the 2025 active-power target 50 MW and cut FY25 capex from $20–23bn to $12–14bn; the delayed sites landed in Q1-26.Q3-25 and Q4-25 calls
2030: “at least 8 GW”. Contracted 4.2 GW plus >1.5 GW of powered land, options and LOIs is ~6 GW; the model carries 7 GW by end-2030 and leaves the rest unmodelled.Q2-26 call · tracker pipeline
~850k GPUs by Dec 2026 on 1.85 GW active. The company reported >250k GPUs at end-2024 on 360 MW; density per MW falls as Blackwell and Rubin racks replace Hopper.10-K FY25 · model densities

Six-year book life. Technology equipment is depreciated over six years (five before 2023); management points to A100s re-contracted into 2029 and H100 pricing within 10% of a year earlier.10-K Note 2 · Q4-25 and Q2-26 calls

Vera Rubin from Q4-27. Meta’s $21bn order and Jane Street’s $6bn commitment are the first Vera Rubin deployments; CoreWeave took delivery of the first VR NVL72 rack in June 2026.8-K 9 Apr 2026 · 8-K 15 Apr 2026

Backlog, not ARR. CoreWeave reports revenue backlog — RPO plus other committed amounts — $104bn at 30 June, 41% recognised within 24 months, >$25bn more signed in early Q3. The chart converts the same contracts into a run-rate on active capacity.Q2-26 10-Q · 11 Aug call

Tenor sets the price, and CoreWeave sells the cheapest tenor. The same Blackwell megawatt clears at $9.7–16.5m on 5-year paper, $20–25m on 1–3 years and $40–50m on 3–6 months. 98% of CoreWeave’s revenue is 5-year fixed take-or-pay, priced cost-plus to a target margin, so its average per MW grows ~20% from 2027 to 2030 against +65% on the owner-operator pages, even after the July +25% list step. Its ~$10m 2023–26 paper is locked to 2030–31 and is still 23% of the 2030 fleet.pricing-trajectory research, 8 Sep 2026 · Q2-26 call · 10-K

Signed vs contracted. Signed run-rate reaches ~$44bn by early 2029 when the 4.2 GW contracted footprint is active. Everything after is options, LOIs and pipeline the model assumes signs 5-year take-or-pay at $14.5–15m per MW as it energises, 10% kept for spot. The owner’s hypothesis that new-generation pricing lifts the average faster is carried as the high case: $157 a share on the old $14–17.5m ladder.90% of unsigned capacity contracted · research 8 Sep 2026

Success-based capex. Contracted revenue more than covers capex within the contract term; each deployment is financed by a self-amortising delayed-draw term loan plus prepayments. DDTL 4.0 ($8.5bn, SOFR+225 / 5.9% fixed, non-recourse, A3) advances 90% of cost; DDTL 5.5 ($2.6bn, SOFR+550) finances 3-year contracts.8-Ks 30 Mar, 15 May, 7 Aug 2026

“Weighted-average cost of debt down almost 300 bps in a year.” $35.6bn of debt at 30 June: DDTLs $13.6bn, senior notes $10.0bn at 9–9.75%, converts $6.6bn at 1.75%, OEM financing $4.8bn. Interest ran $640m in Q2 against $1.51bn of adjusted EBITDA.Q2-26 10-Q Note 8 · 11 Aug call

The catch: prepayments are 15–25% of contract value and lenders advance 90% only against signed take-or-pay. Unsigned capacity needs ~$16.5m of equity per MW — or, as in 2025, the NVIDIA backstop and equity placements ($2bn at $87.20, $1bn at $109).424B4 · 8-Ks 23 Jan, 15 Apr 2026

Rent is the cost. Adjusted EBITDA margin 56–59% after rent, power and data-centre staff (the quarterly table runs at 57%); management puts some scaled contracts in a ~70% zone, and the per-MW economics use 60%. Core Scientific charges ~$120/kW-month ($1.4m per MW-yr), Applied Digital ~$150 ($1.8m).Q2-26 release · lessor filings

Capex is $30–33m per active MW and rising. Management capex ÷ active MW added gives $30m for FY25 and $25m for H1-26; component inflation is passed through in contract pricing since Q1-26.10-K FY25 · Q1-26 and Q2-26 calls

Maintenance, not replacement. Refresh as a tray swap at ~55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr spares: $5.5m per MW-yr on $33m of silicon. A tenant keeps $2m of every $14m today; the multiple is what the market’s +6%/yr does to that over five years.model · peer 10-Ks

Some equity, not none. $3bn of placements in 2026 against $37bn of capex. Base: 10% of the 2027–30 build plus the residual the flywheel cannot cover, at an assumed $90 — the bridge shows the count; the summary table shows the quarters.8-Ks · 11 Aug call

The multiple is the swing. At $14m per MW and 60% after rent, $1 of run-rate is worth ~2.75× — well under IREN’s 4.06× because the tenant pays rent and earns half the revenue per MW on the same silicon. Signed contracts never escalate; they reprice when they end.contracted 5-yr at 10.5% · spot at 13%
EPS is the long-run anchor. A six-year book flatters CoreWeave’s earnings relative to IREN’s five. Pick your multiple.after the raise

footer.model: Compute/Value tracker, CoreWeave ramp drafted 4 Sep 2026 by the §6e playbook. Ramp: company-reported active power as billing IT MW; 2026 to the >1.85 GW guide, 2027 to >3 GW, 2028 the 4.2 GW contracted footprint, 2029 options and LOIs, 2030 rumored pipeline to 7 GW; rates per active MW-yr $10m on the signed book rising to $17.5m on 2030 vintages, 10% of unsigned capacity at $35m spot, 90% contracted. Capex per active MW: $30m Blackwell, +10% on 2027 orders, $38m Rubin, $45m next-gen; no shell — every site is leased with rent inside the 60% EBITDA margin. Steady-state: $14m revenue per active MW-yr, 60% EBITDA, $33m GPUs, 21% tax, 10.5% WACC; market $/MW +6%/yr for five years then flat; contracted MW reprice at 5-yr renewals, spot at 13%; refresh 55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr; 10% of the 2027–30 build in equity at $90; operating cash funds the build first, prepayments next, debt within lenders’ cover, equity for the rest. Honest-base items: prepayments credited back in the final year of each contract with the balance owed at 2030 deducted at PV; the $6.6bn of converts as equity at the model’s 2030 price with capped calls netted; restricted cash counted. Value = 2030 EV less net debt ex converts and prepayments owed, discounted to today, over the diluted count.

capexBasis: GPUs + ancillaries per active MW by vintage: $30m Blackwell (derived $25-37m from management capex ÷ active MW added, FY25 and H1-26), +10% on 2027 orders, Rubin ~$38m, next-gen ~$45m; no shell capex — every data centre is leased (10-K: “we lease all of our existing data centers”; $35.5bn of signed-not-commenced leases at 30-Jun-26)
